segments.line: What if you could see something about other
that they'd never know you could see?
Hey, nice sweater.
Oh, hey. Thanks.
I invented the lifesight detector.
It's my own design. No one else has one.
When I wear it, a small number appears above each person's head.
A dark pill with a coloured outline,
almost touching the top of their head.
It shows how many lives they've already lived.
Reincarnation. Call it what you will.
The number ticks down when a life is spent.
Used up. Passed.
Look at Mr. Harwick, the history teacher.
Seven lives. He's seen a lot.
You've lived twelve times.
That's incredible.
Three lives, Jordan. You've got plenty left.
I guess I'm due for a good one then.
Is this real? Is there actual evidence for reincarnation?
The device I built is my own invention.
It doesn't measure anything scientific.
Dr. Ian Stevenson, a psychiatrist at the University of Virginia,
documented over 2,500 cases of children
worldwide who described detailed memories of
of previous personalities.
Part one.
